research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official Ofcom, BDUK/DSIT and GOV.UK planning/digital-infrastructure sources checked on 25 July 2026. Coverage snapshots, planned deployments, OMR classifications, Project Gigabit management information, address-checker outputs, mobile predictions and planning guidance remain at their published scope. They are not parcel-level guaranteed service, build completion, operator contract, legal access, mast consent, planning permission or Future Growth score accuracy.

source_facts.fact: As of January 2026 Ofcom reports full fibre at 24.9 million UK homes (82%) and gigabit-capable broadband at 27.1 million homes (89%).
source_facts.gate: UK residential availability is not an address-level service guarantee or installed connection.

source_facts.fact: If operator plans are realised, Ofcom projects full fibre to 28.1 million homes and gigabit-capable coverage to 29 million homes by January 2029.
source_facts.gate: Forward-looking operator plans are not delivered infrastructure and must remain conditional.

source_facts.fact: Spring 2026 reports predicted good 4G geographic coverage from all MNOs across 84% of UK landmass and at least one MNO across 96%; 5G SA outside-premises coverage ranges 49% to 85% across three deployed MNOs.
source_facts.gate: Predicted coverage is not measured parcel signal, indoor service guarantee or network performance commitment.

source_facts.fact: The checker disclaimer says its data comes from the January OMR published in June 2026, is updated periodically and cannot guarantee complete address-status accuracy.
source_facts.gate: Checker output must not be promoted to a legally guaranteed build or connection date.

source_facts.source: BDUK Project Gigabit monthly management information
source_facts.fact: July 2026 contract reporting is a snapshot with ingestion lag and explicitly says it should not be used to assess contractual milestones.
source_facts.gate: Contracted/built management-information rows are not milestone compliance or parcel service evidence.

source_facts.fact: Planning policy supports high-quality electronic communications including 5G and full fibre while applications still require planning evidence and applicable permissions.
source_facts.gate: Policy support is not automatic planning permission or Code-right access to a site.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ofcom full-fibre availability January 2026
official_measurement_examples.fact: 24.9 million UK residential premises, 82% of 30.5 million homes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ofcom gigabit-capable availability January 2026
official_measurement_examples.fact: 27.1 million UK homes, 89%, up from 87% in July 2025.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ofcom 4G geographic coverage January 2026
official_measurement_examples.fact: Predicted good 4G geographic coverage from all MNOs reaches 84% of UK landmass; at least one MNO remains 96%.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ofcom 5G standalone coverage January 2026
official_measurement_examples.fact: Outside-premises 5G SA coverage ranges from 49% to 85% across the three MNOs that had deployed it.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ofcom planned fixed networks to January 2029
official_measurement_examples.fact: If plans are realised, full fibre could reach 28.1 million homes (92%) and gigabit-capable coverage 29 million homes (95%).

official_measurement_examples.name: Ofcom planned FWA mast expansion
official_measurement_examples.fact: Around 6,950 geographically distinct FWA masts are planned or set to be upgraded between January 2026 and January 2029.

official_measurement_examples.name: BDUK annual subsidised delivery 2025-26
official_measurement_examples.fact: BDUK estimates 192,570 premises received gigabit-capable coverage through subsidy in 2025/26, cumulative 1,418,410 since programme launch.

official_measurement_examples.name: BDUK address checker disclaimer July 2026
official_measurement_examples.fact: Address status uses the January OMR published in June 2026; supplier plans can change and BDUK does not guarantee complete accuracy.

core_rules: national broadband availability is not an address-level service guarantee
residential coverage percentage must not be substituted for business-premises coverage
full-fibre availability is not full-fibre take-up
gigabit-capable availability is not a contracted retail service
a premises passed by a network is not necessarily connected or activated
address-checker output is informational and not a legally binding delivery commitment
BDUK OMR classification is a subsidy-control planning view and not a connection contract
an OMR future-commercial-plan status is not evidence that build has completed
OMR data can change when suppliers revise plans and must remain date-versioned
a UPRN missing from a BDUK premises base must not be inferred to have no broadband
AddressBase epoch limitations can exclude new, demolished or reclassified premises
Project Gigabit contracted premises are not the same measure as BDUK official-statistics delivered premises
Project Gigabit built management information must not be used as contractual milestone compliance
management-information ingestion lag must be preserved when interpreting monthly tables
revisions to supplier administrative data must not be converted into physical build reversals without evidence
monthly BDUK contract snapshots must not be treated as a continuous live feed
public subsidy delivery is not evidence of retail product availability from every provider
BDUK intervention status is not planning permission for network works
Ofcom Connected Nations is a coverage snapshot and not a planning allocation
Ofcom planned deployment data is forward-looking and conditional on operator plans
planned deployment confidence is not physical construction completion
planned full-fibre coverage must not be represented as current coverage
planned FWA mast count is not mast planning consent or landowner agreement
network overbuild can cause planned premises counts to overlap and must not be summed as unique new homes
coverage from at least one MNO must remain distinct from coverage from all MNOs
4G geographic landmass coverage is not indoor premises coverage
5G SA coverage must remain distinct from 5G NSA and overall 5G
mobile coverage predictions are not guaranteed measured signal at a parcel
Ofcom High Confidence and Very High Confidence levels must remain distinct
crowdsourced mobile performance is not the same evidence type as operator coverage prediction
postal-district performance must not be downscaled to a single address
trees buildings terrain and indoor construction can alter local mobile performance
a broadband universal-service right to request is not an automatic free installation
the USO minimum-speed definition is not equivalent to gigabit-capable service
satellite affordability can affect USO eligibility without creating fixed-network infrastructure
full-fibre network competition counts do not guarantee provider choice at a specific address
two-network or three-network national estimates are not parcel-level provider counts
rural and urban national coverage rates must not be assigned to individual parcels
local-authority coverage statistics are not parcel geometry evidence
communications planning policy support is not automatic planning permission
permitted development rights still have limits conditions and notification or prior-approval rules
prior approval is not identical to full planning permission
Electronic Communications Code rights are not created merely because a network is desirable
Code rights require applicable agreement or legal process and must not be inferred from coverage plans
network operator need must not be confused with legal land access
NPPF support for 5G and full fibre does not override environmental or heritage constraints
use of existing masts is policy guidance and not evidence that a specific mast has capacity
a planned small-cell programme does not prove installation at a street asset
publicly owned asset availability is not operator tenancy or wayleave consent
DCIA pilot activity is not nationwide production deployment
wireless strategy objectives are not funded build commitments at a parcel
planning consultations and calls for evidence must not be represented as enacted planning law
historic planning guidance must be checked against current NPPF before parcel use
coverage statistics must preserve their January 2026 measurement date
July 2026 BDUK monthly publication date must not be confused with the underlying snapshot date
future January 2029 coverage projections must not be labelled 2026 current coverage
percentage-point changes must not be converted into unverified premises counts
national figures must not be downscaled using parcel area or postcode population without an official method
retail broadband speed is not guaranteed by network technology label alone
advertised maximum speed is not measured busy-hour performance
network availability is not resilience or outage evidence
mobile coverage is not emergency-service coverage unless the source explicitly measures it
telecom infrastructure proximity is not legal access to ducts poles or chambers
digital connectivity evidence must not be converted directly into land value or Future Growth score
NO_DATA must remain unknown rather than no-service or no-risk
